segments.he: בעת המחלוקת מהרב מסווראן על מוהרנ"ת ז"ל שהציקו למהרנ"ת ז"ל ענה ואמר "פין מיר וועט בלייבען אשאנק (מגדל) מיט ספרים. אין פין מיהם וועט בלייבען אשאנק מיט פלעשיר. וכן היה שממוהרנ"ת נשאר מגדל מלא ספרים כתבי יד כל הלק"ה וכו' וכו'. וממנו לא נשאר כלום רק מגדל עם בקבוקים כי הי' חולה והי' שותה יין וכו' ונשאר מגדל מלא בקבוקים כידוע לכל.
segments.en:
Concerning the holy Tzaddik Reb Yitzchak Leib the Great, a disciple of Rabbainu — who had previously been a great performer of wonders, using practical Kabbalah, famous throughout the world for this. The holy Tzaddik Reb Nachum of Chernobyl heard of him, passed through his town on a journey, and caused him to fall into a great spiritual descent.

Rabbainu immediately traveled that same route and passed by Reb Yitzchak Leib. Rabbainu said to himself: "Aykuft yenm arop tsu vorfn? Aykuft yenm oyf tsi haybn!" [Should I throw him further down? I should lift him up!] Reb Yitzchak Leib prostrated himself before Rabbainu, begging to be received as a disciple. Rabbainu received him on condition that he perform no more wonders, and that throughout that year he travel with Rabbainu to all the places where he had previously performed wonders — and at each one declare that he is not a rebbe. And so he did — always pointing only to Rabbainu as the true Rebbe.

Once Rabbainu was on the road and the time for Minchah arrived but there was no water for immersion. Rabbainu was distressed. Reb Yitzchak Leib said he could — with Rabbainu's permission — make a circle with his staff and a spring of water would appear. Rabbainu gave permission, he made the circle, a spring appeared, and Rabbainu immersed himself. Reb Yitzchak Leib also wanted to immerse. Rabbainu said to him: "Du nisht" [Not you]. A similar story is told about the Ba'al Shem Tov.

After Rabbainu's passing, when there was controversy among our fellowship about what the Shpole Zeide [the Elder] had done, our fellows asked Reb Yitzchak Leib why he was silent. He answered: within the first year after a Tzaddik's passing he did not want the Elder to also die — for it is written in the books of the Kabbalists that in the year a Tzaddik departs, there is joy and celebration throughout all the worlds [and he did not wish to cut that time short].

After the year, Reb Yitzchak Leib was traveling on a wagon with other members of our fellowship. They got off the wagon and Reb Yitzchak Leib struck the horse with his hand — a mighty blow — and directed a holy Name [as is known, when one wishes to accomplish something through practical Kabbalah in this manner, one must perform an action upon a living creature]. The horse died instantly. He declared: "At this moment, the Elder has died." And so it was. One of our fellowship told me that he knew members of our fellowship who had been on that wagon — and they told him that they were compelled to carry the wagon home themselves, for the horse had died as described.
